shared_elements: crouching/prone figure in profile with a bird-like head and long curved beak
paired or repeated bird-headed figures aligned in a row
curvilinear low-relief outlined forms with plain interiors
carving fitted to a curved, irregular rock surface
justification: Both surfaces show the same distinctive motif: a crouching profile figure with a long-beaked bird head, rendered as a smooth outlined low-relief silhouette without interior detail, repeated in series and accompanied by spiral/ring discs. The main difference is in composition: A combines the bird-headed figures with additional discrete symbols (a large ring-and-boss, elongated paddle-like forms, an oval sign) distributed over a shaped anthropomorphic body, whereas B is a denser row of overlapping bird-headed figures with spirals filling the natural rock face.
